dedupe_keys.name: nasa climate adaptation plan may 2024 resilience assessments of space centres and launch facilities

description: NASA's Climate Adaptation Plan of May 2024 sets out how the agency assesses and reduces climate risk to its space centres, launch sites, laboratories and missions. The Mission Support Directorate and the Office of Strategic Infrastructure lead it, and it commits NASA to integrate adaptation into master plans, programmes and operations. Coverage is the whole agency, with 5,031 owned buildings on about 135,000 acres. Its Agency Resilience Framework was completed in 2023, and Center Resilience Assessments have been finished at Johnson, Kennedy, Goddard and Wallops, and Langley, with results used to prioritise facility renewal and repair. Format and access: a 33-page PDF on sustainability.gov, free to read; its first 14 pages were read. Licence: US Government work, no restriction stated. Caveats: it is a planning document without the underlying assessment data, and later plan versions may differ. It supports climate adaptation, hazard exposure and capacity planning for space ground infrastructure. A related catalogue record is the UK space weather reasonable worst case scenarios study, which covers a different hazard for space infrastructure.
